principles.rule: Conceptual integrity is the most important consideration in design: keep the system coherent under one unifying idea rather than a pile of uncoordinated features.
checks: a single coherent concept guides the design
features added consistently, not ad hoc

principles.rule: Plan to throw one away: treat the first cut as a prototype and grow the system iteratively/incrementally; expect and plan for change.
Beware the second-system effect: when rewriting or extending, resist over-engineering and feature bloat from ideas deferred earlier.
Representation is the essence of programming: choose the right data structures first; good data design makes algorithms simple.
checks: data model designed deliberately before/alongside logic

principles.rule: Design the bugs out: prevent defects through clear design rather than relying on later debugging.
checks: clear structure that prevents whole classes of errors

principles.rule: No silver bullet: manage essential complexity through thoughtful design; do not expect a single tool/technique/framework to solve inherent complexity.
checks: complexity addressed by design, not by tool worship

principles.rule: Favor self-documenting programs: structure and naming should explain the code; keep necessary written specs precise.
